heading: Hot plates, deep pockets
body: Two heated grids cook the batter from both sides at once.
points: The grid makes pockets that crisp up
Steam escapes from the sides as it cooks
Most irons have a ready light

parts.name: Handle
parts.text: Lifts the lid and latches it shut. Always use the handle, because the metal around the plates gets very hot.

parts.name: Top grid plate
parts.text: Cooks the upper side of the waffle. Its raised squares press down into the batter to make the deep pockets and crisp edges.

parts.name: Bottom grid plate
parts.text: Holds the batter and browns the underside. Grease it lightly so the waffle lifts out cleanly.

parts.name: Ready light
parts.text: Tells you when the plates are hot enough. Pour the batter only after it turns green, so the outside crisps right away.

switch.name: Power switch
switch.text: Turns the heat on and off. Switch it on first and let the iron preheat before you pour any batter.
switch.tip: Try it: flip the switch on the iron and watch the plates heat up.
switch.heatingText: The light is red while the iron heats up. When it turns green, the iron is ready for batter.

narration: A waffle iron is two heated grids that close around the batter.
The grid shape creates deep pockets with lots of crisp edges.
As the batter cooks, steam escapes. When the steam slows down, your waffle is nearly done.
